working_title: Common decline, divergent endpoints: multiscale demography across Antarctic penguin breeding islands
one_sentence_claim: Across neighboring externally subsidized penguin breeding islands, a shared long-term regional decline resolves into heterogeneous local ecological endpoints; simple tested climate/weather formulations do not identify the divergence mechanism, and within-island effective colony number remains conditionally associated with next-year growth but is not a robust held-out predictor.

evidence_roles.apbp_local_network: local endpoint context: persistence, vacancy/extinction and non-island species replacement
evidence_roles.lter_five_island_synchrony: regional demographic background; synchrony contrast is descriptive and interpreted within established timescale-dependent theory
evidence_roles.seaice_and_weather: prospective falsification of bounded simple environmental formulations
evidence_roles.neff_year_block_permutation: primary uncertainty diagnostic that removes robust predictive support (p=0.26224)
evidence_roles.neff_mechanical_coupling: fixed stylized sensitivity showing shared census error does not readily generate the observed coefficient
evidence_roles.external_torgersen_mapping: phenomenon-level independent evidence for real habitat-structured subcolony attrition

primary_claims: The five focal Adelie islands share a strong long-term decline, while local annual dynamics and endpoints differ.
The long-term/annual synchrony contrast is consistent with known timescale-dependent synchrony and is not a novelty claim by itself.
Nearby breeding sites terminate in heterogeneous ecological states, including persistence at low abundance, local extinction/vacancy and species replacement.
The tested annual and low-frequency sea-ice-duration and annual snowfall-by-habitat formulations fail their frozen directional/predictive rules.
N_eff has a positive conditional standardized coefficient (+0.1168), but its +0.00103 held-out MSE gain is null-compatible under synchronized year-block permutation (p=0.26224).
Fixed Poisson and Gamma-Poisson count-error coupling simulations do not generate an observed-scale N_eff coefficient; this retains the coefficient only as a bounded conditional association.
Independent Torgersen mapping shows habitat-structured subcolony attrition, but no colony-code/GIS polygon crosswalk exists.
prohibited_claims: N_eff robustly predicts held-out future growth
PC1 96.4% is a novel synchrony discovery
sea ice or snow are ecologically unimportant
simple shared census error has been empirically ruled out beyond the fixed stylized simulations
mapped Torgersen habitat attrition validates the exact LTER N_eff metric
all Palmer breeding sites follow the same species-replacement pathway
manuscript_order: system: externally subsidized breeding patches separate marine resources from terrestrial reproduction
known theory: synchrony is timescale-dependent; the five-island pattern defines analysis scale rather than novelty
regional background: common long-term Adelie decline
local ecological outcome: persistence, extinction/vacancy and replacement differ among nearby breeding sites
bounded mechanisms: simple sea-ice-duration and snowfall formulations fail prospectively
local association: N_eff beta remains positive but held-out predictive gain fails block-permutation uncertainty
mechanical diagnostic: fixed shared-count-error models do not generate observed-scale beta
external triangulation: Torgersen has real habitat-structured subcolony attrition
synthesis: regional demographic direction and local ecological fate are distinct dimensions
terminal_development_rule: Do not open new climate windows, weather months, topology metrics, colony-size thresholds or count-error model grids for the core paper. New science must be independent spatial crosswalk/replication or a separate project.
